name: Panasonic LUMIX S 14-28mm F4-5.6 MACRO
notes: Model number S-R1428. Announced at CES in January 2023 alongside the LUMIX S5II; Panasonic North America gave $799.99 with availability at the end of March 2023 (Europe: February 2023, EUR 999 / GBP 879.99). Panasonic lists 14 elements in 10 groups: 1 aspherical ED element (counted here under both aspherical and low-dispersion), 1 aspherical, 3 ED and 1 UHR element. Panasonic gives one closest focusing distance (0.15 m) for the whole zoom range and one minimum aperture (F22), used for both ends. Maximum magnification is 0.25x at 14mm and 0.5x at 28mm. Panasonic's spec sheet lists 7 diaphragm blades (circular aperture). No O.I.S. in the name: the lens has no optical stabilisation and relies on camera IBIS. The AF drive type and whether the barrel extends when zooming did not appear in accessible official snippets, so autofocus is null and zoomMechanism/focusMechanism are omitted. Dimensions are Panasonic's maximum diameter x length from the lens tip to the mount base side.
famousFor: A small, light ultra-wide zoom for the L-Mount that doubles as a close-up lens, reaching 0.5x magnification at 28mm with a 15 cm minimum focus distance, at a much lower price and weight than constant-f/2.8 ultra-wides.
strengths: Very compact and light at about 345 g
Unusual 0.5x close-up capability at 28mm
Good centre sharpness from f/4, best around f/5.6-f/8
Takes standard 77mm screw-in filters despite the 14mm wide end
weaknesses: Slow variable f/4-5.6 aperture limits low-light and astro use
Some residual barrel distortion at 14mm, even with in-camera correction
Short 2x zoom range
bestFor: Landscapes and travel photography with a light kit
Interiors and architecture in tight spaces
Wide-angle close-ups of flowers and small subjects with their surroundings
Vlogging and handheld wide video on stabilised LUMIX bodies

name: Panasonic LUMIX S PRO 50mm F1.4
autofocus: Double focus system (linear motor + stepping motor)
notes: Model number S-X50. Panasonic's pages give 13 elements in 11 groups with 2 aspherical and 3 ED elements, an 11-blade circular aperture, a 77mm filter, approx. 0.15x maximum magnification, dust/splash resistance and freeze resistance to -10 C, and a double focus system combining a linear motor and a stepping motor. Weight (955 g), announcement date (1 February 2019, with the LUMIX S1/S1R) and the $2,299 launch price come from DPReview/B&H (non-official) because they did not appear in accessible official snippets. Minimum aperture, closest focusing distance and the lens diameter could not be verified and are left null; DPReview gives a length of 130 mm, but because the diameter is unverified the whole dimensionsMm field is left null. No O.I.S. in the name: no optical stabilisation (relies on camera IBIS). Little review detail was available for this lens: the descriptive text leans on DPReview's 'reference lens' description and Panasonic's own sharpness claims, and no review assessment of AF speed was found, so the AF strength states only the mechanism.
famousFor: The launch 'reference' prime of Panasonic's full-frame LUMIX S system, built to resolve the S1R's high-resolution sensor from centre to edge, and known as one of the largest and heaviest 50mm f/1.4 lenses on the market.
strengths: High sharpness from the centre to the edges of the frame
11-blade circular aperture for smooth, round out-of-focus highlights
Double focus system driven by a linear motor and a stepping motor
Dust- and splash-resistant, freeze-resistant to -10 C
weaknesses: Very heavy and bulky for a 50mm f/1.4 (about 955 g)
Expensive at launch compared with other 50mm f/1.4 lenses
No optical stabilisation
bestFor: High-resolution portraits and people photography with shallow depth of field
Low-light events and weddings
Studio and product work on high-megapixel L-Mount bodies
Cinematic video with a natural standard field of view

name: Panasonic LUMIX S 50mm F1.8
notes: Model number S-S50. Second of Panasonic's matched F1.8 primes (shared 67mm filter and near-identical size/control layout). Panasonic's specifications give 9 elements in 8 groups (3 aspherical, 1 ED, 1 UHR), 9-blade circular aperture, F22 minimum aperture, 0.45 m closest focus, 0.14x maximum magnification, approx. 300 g (without caps and hood) and 73.6 x 82.0 mm (length from lens tip to mount base). Announced 1 June 2021; Panasonic North America listed it at $449.99 with July 2021 availability. The linear AF motor is stated on Panasonic India's official store listing and in Panasonic's LUMIX blog on the F1.8 prime series. No O.I.S.: relies on camera IBIS.
famousFor: Panasonic's affordable, lightweight standard prime for full-frame L-Mount bodies, part of a matched F1.8 prime family that shares one size, weight class and 67mm filter so video shooters can swap lenses without rebalancing a gimbal.
strengths: Light (about 300 g) and compact, yet dust- and splash-resistant
Sharp with quick, silent linear-motor autofocus
Low distortion and good flare control
Rounded 9-blade aperture for smooth bokeh; low focus breathing for video
weaknesses: Noticeable vignetting wide open (largely gone by f/2.8)
Some purple fringing in strong backlight
Modest 0.14x close-focus magnification and no focus limiter
bestFor: Everyday walk-around and street photography
Budget portraits with background blur
Gimbal video alongside the other LUMIX S F1.8 primes
Travel photography where weight matters

name: Panasonic LUMIX S 85mm F1.8
notes: Model number S-S85. First of Panasonic's matched F1.8 primes (same 73.6 x 82.0 mm size and 67mm filter as the S 50mm F1.8). Panasonic's specifications give 9 elements in 8 groups with 2 ED elements, a 9-blade circular aperture, 0.8 m closest focus, 0.13x maximum magnification and approx. 355 g; the F22 minimum aperture is stated only in the title of Panasonic India's official store listing (treat with slight caution), and the linear AF motor there and in Panasonic's LUMIX blog on the F1.8 prime series. Announced 4 November 2020. The US launch price of $599 is as reported by DPReview/PetaPixel (Panasonic UK: GBP 599.99); the exact official US figure (possibly $599.99) was not seen in accessible official snippets. US availability was quoted as mid-December 2020, although some sources mention January 2021. specialElements lists only the ED elements that Panasonic names. No O.I.S.: relies on camera IBIS.
famousFor: A compact, affordable 85mm portrait prime for L-Mount that reviewers found sharp from centre to edge even at f/1.8, with smooth bokeh, excellent flare control and almost zero distortion.
strengths: Excellent centre and edge sharpness from f/1.8
Smooth, softly graduated bokeh from a rounded 9-blade aperture
Very well controlled flare and virtually no distortion
Light (about 355 g), weather-resistant and fairly priced
weaknesses: f/1.8 gives less background blur and light than f/1.4 or f/1.2 portrait lenses
No optical stabilisation
Limited close-up ability (0.8 m minimum focus, 0.13x)
bestFor: Head-and-shoulders portraits with soft backgrounds
Weddings and events from a discreet distance
Stage and indoor performances in low light
Interview and B-camera video framing alongside the other S F1.8 primes

name: Panasonic LUMIX S 100mm F2.8 MACRO
notes: Model number S-E100. Announced at CES in January 2024 (Panasonic North America: $999.99, available end of January 2024). Panasonic calls it the world's smallest and lightest medium-telephoto fixed-focal-length macro lens (Panasonic's claim at launch). Panasonic's specifications give 13 elements in 11 groups (3 aspherical, 2 UED, 1 ED), 9-blade circular aperture, F22 minimum aperture, 0.204 m closest focus, 1x magnification, approx. 298 g, 73.6 x 82.0 mm and a 67mm filter; it shares size, filter thread and control layout with the S F1.8 prime series. UED is Panasonic's 'Ultra Extra-Low Dispersion' glass, normalised here as super-low-dispersion. Autofocus uses a newly developed Dual Phase Linear Motor. No O.I.S.: relies on camera IBIS.
famousFor: Launched as the world's smallest and lightest medium-telephoto macro lens (Panasonic's claim) at about 298 g, with life-size 1:1 magnification, a new dual phase linear AF motor and the same compact body and 67mm filter as Panasonic's F1.8 primes.
strengths: Remarkably small and light for a full-frame 1:1 macro
Sharp from corner to corner even at f/2.8
Fast, quiet, precise autofocus that stays usable at 1:1
Focus breathing well suppressed at normal subject distances, good for video
weaknesses: Short working distance at 1:1 compared with rival 100-105mm macros
No optical stabilisation
Angle of view narrows noticeably when focusing into the macro range
bestFor: Life-size macro of flowers, insects and small details
Product and jewellery photography
Head-and-shoulders portraits with a compact kit
Close-up B-roll video alongside the S F1.8 primes

name: Panasonic LUMIX S PRO 70-200mm F2.8 O.I.S.
autofocus: Double focus system with double-magnet linear motors
notes: Model number S-E70200. Announced 6 November 2019 (together with the S PRO 16-35mm F4) and on sale from January 2020; Panasonic North America gave a price of $2,599. Panasonic's pages give 22 elements in 17 groups with 2 UED and 3 ED elements, an 11-blade circular aperture, 82mm filter, approx. 0.21x maximum magnification and approx. 1,570 g excluding caps, hood and the removable tripod mount (the tripod mount adds approx. 230 g); the F22 minimum aperture is stated only in the title of Panasonic India's official store listing (treat with slight caution). Panasonic describes a double focus system (two focus groups) driven by double-magnet linear motors, with three focus buttons and a focus-clutch mechanism for instant AF/MF switching.

Focus clutch for instant AF/MF switching plus three focus buttons
weaknesses: Heavier than rival 70-200mm f/2.8 zooms (about 1.57 kg without tripod mount)
Expensive
Modest 0.21x close-up magnification
bestFor: Indoor sports and action in dim arenas
Wedding ceremonies and events from a distance
Stage performances and concerts
Tight head-and-shoulders portraits with compressed backgrounds

name: Panasonic LUMIX S 28-200mm F4-7.1 MACRO O.I.S.
notes: Model number S-R28200. Announced February 2024 as the first wide-to-tele all-in-one zoom for LUMIX S, on sale from the end of April 2024; the $899 US price is as reported by DPReview/PetaPixel (Panasonic UK/EU: GBP 899 / EUR 999). Panasonic calls it the world's smallest and lightest long zoom lens (its launch claim). Panasonic's pages give 17 elements in 13 groups including 1 aspherical, 4 ED and 1 UHR element, a 9-blade circular aperture, 67mm filter, approx. 413 g and 77.3 x 93.4 mm (at the 28mm, retracted position); closest focus is 0.14 m at 28mm, where the maximum magnification of 0.5x is reached. Categorised as standard-zoom because it starts at a standard 28mm wide angle (it is an all-in-one travel superzoom). Dust-, splash- and freeze-resistant with a fluorine front coating.
famousFor: The first all-in-one travel zoom in Panasonic's LUMIX S range, launched as the world's smallest and lightest full-frame long zoom (Panasonic's claim) at 413 g and 93.4 mm long, with a 0.5x half-life-size close-up ability at 28mm.

Ghosting and flare with bright light sources
bestFor: One-lens travel photography
Family events and day trips where changing lenses is impractical
Casual close-ups of flowers and food at 28mm

name: Panasonic LEICA DG VARIO-ELMAR 100-400mm F4.0-6.3 II ASPH. POWER O.I.S.
notes: Model number H-RSA100400; the II version of the 2016 H-RS100400, announced 12 September 2023 alongside the LUMIX G9II. 100-400mm on Micro Four Thirds gives a 200-800mm full-frame-equivalent field of view, hence the super-telephoto category. Panasonic's pages give 20 elements in 13 groups with 1 aspherical ED element (counted here under both aspherical and low-dispersion), 1 UED and 2 ED elements, a 1.3 m closest focusing distance (one value, used for both ends), a maximum magnification of approx. 0.25x (0.5x in 35mm-camera equivalent), approx. 985 g excluding caps, hood and the external tripod mount, and a length of approx. 171.5 mm (lens tip to mount base). Unlike the first version it is compatible with Panasonic's 1.4x and 2x teleconverters, and gains freeze-resistant sealing (per B&H). A 'zoom limiter switch' and 'zoom lock ring' taken from the B&H listing could not be confirmed from any Panasonic source, so the descriptive text does not claim them; nor does it rate image quality with the teleconverters, because no review of the II version with a teleconverter is among the sources. The 72mm filter and 9-blade rounded diaphragm come from B&H's listing (non-official). B&H lists the lens at $1,597.99, but this could not be confirmed as the launch MSRP, so launchPrice is null. Minimum aperture, diameter (so dimensionsMm), AF drive type and a CIPA stabilisation rating were not found and are left null. The lens has POWER O.I.S. and works with LUMIX Dual I.S. bodies.
famousFor: A Leica-certified Micro Four Thirds super-telephoto zoom giving 200-800mm-equivalent reach in a hand-holdable package with POWER O.I.S.; the II version adds teleconverter compatibility for even longer reach and freeze-resistant sealing.
strengths: Huge 200-800mm-equivalent reach in a package light enough to hand-hold
Works with Panasonic's 1.4x and 2x teleconverters (new in the II version)
Built-in POWER O.I.S. for handheld shooting at long focal lengths
Dust-, splash- and freeze-resistant build
weaknesses: Slow f/6.3 maximum aperture at 400mm limits low-light shooting
Heavy for a Micro Four Thirds lens (about 985 g)
bestFor: Birds and wildlife that cannot be approached
Field sports and motorsport from the sidelines
Airshows and plane spotting
Close-ups of butterflies and dragonflies from 1.3 m away
